entries.label: Two
entries.ambiguity: The invariant is the number of marks. The repeated arrangement could instead suggest a pair, symmetry, or equal spacing.

entries.label: Inside
entries.ambiguity: A closed boundary contains a mark in each positive example. A 2D diagram cannot by itself distinguish containment from projected overlap.

entries.label: Change of position
entries.ambiguity: Successive frames suggest one object changing position. A reader may see separate objects or infer the reverse order. Frame order depends on the primer.

entries.label: Earth
entries.ambiguity: The two views show the same planet from different perspectives. The shared shape may suggest the class of planets instead of this individual body.

entries.label: Plant
entries.ambiguity: The fern and tree show two examples of plants. Backgrounds and different scales make it unclear which pictured feature carries the label.

entries.label: Human
entries.ambiguity: Groups in varied settings show multiple humans. The examples cannot independently teach species membership, cultural roles, or the range of human variation.

entries.label: Outside
entries.ambiguity: The mark is separated from the closed boundary in both examples. It could be interpreted as distance or exclusion. Try touching and overlapping cases separately.

entries.label: Equal length
entries.ambiguity: The segments have different positions but cover the same number of intervals. A reader may infer parallelism or equal placement instead of length.

entries.label: Same position across observations
entries.ambiguity: The mark occupies corresponding positions in the two aligned frames. It could be seen as two separate objects or as repetition without time.

entries.label: Earlier observation
entries.ambiguity: The shorter observation count identifies the earlier frame. Reversed chronology or simple spatial ordering remains plausible without separate demonstrations of elapsed time.

statements.label: Two inside
statements.ambiguity: The trial convention places quantity before relationship. The sequence alone leaves the object type and enclosing boundary implicit.

statements.label: Two move
statements.ambiguity: These examples hold the number constant as positions change. They do not establish tense, agency, cause or simultaneous movement.

statements.label: Two outside
statements.ambiguity: The enclosing boundary acts as the reference. The images do not establish whether the two objects are a group or independent items.

illustrations.two-disks: Two filled disks, spaced apart on one line.
illustrations.two-squares: Two filled squares, one above and left of the other.
illustrations.disk-inside: A disk lies within a rounded rectangle.
illustrations.triangle-inside: A triangle lies within a circle.
illustrations.disk-moves: In the first frame a disk is near the lower left. In the next frame it is near the upper right.
illustrations.square-moves: A square is near the upper right in the first frame and near the lower left in the next.
illustrations.two-disks-inside: Two disks lie within a rounded rectangle.
illustrations.two-triangles-inside: Two triangles lie within a circle.
illustrations.two-disks-move: The first frame has two disks near the bottom. The second has two disks near the top.
illustrations.two-squares-move: The first frame has two squares on its right side. The second has two squares on its left side.
illustrations.disk-outside: A disk is to the left of and entirely outside a rounded rectangle.
illustrations.triangle-outside: A triangle is to the right of and entirely outside a circle.
illustrations.horizontal-equal: Two offset horizontal segments each cover three equally spaced intervals.
illustrations.vertical-equal: Two offset vertical segments each cover three equally spaced intervals.
illustrations.disk-stays: Two successive frames show a disk in the same position within each frame.
illustrations.square-stays: Two successive frames show a square in the same position within each frame.
illustrations.disk-earlier: The first frame, containing a lower disk, is paired with one observation mark. The second frame, containing a higher disk, is paired with two.
illustrations.square-earlier: The first frame, containing an upper square, is paired with two observation marks. The second frame, containing a lower square, is paired with three.
illustrations.two-disks-outside: Two disks are outside a rounded rectangle, one on either side.
illustrations.two-triangles-outside: Two triangles are outside a circle, one above and one below.
